solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In disorder, like soldiers returned from leave

definitions.meaning: jumbled with the rear end placed first
troops whose leave is over go back to the front line

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase as BACK TO (the) FRONT: where soldiers go once leave ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reversed end to end is in a muddle; soldiers returning from leave literally head back to the front.

clue.text: One's found in pubs, a proper lady!

indicators.note: One's is placed inside the word for pubs

parts.note: a bar is a pub, so pubs are BARS
one's written as a plural, ONES

explanation.surface: A remark that a real lady can be met in public houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A baroness is a titled noblewoman, a lady in the formal, rank-holding sense.

clue.text: Rice, for example, entertains British intellectual

indicators.note: to entertain is to take in a guest, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: rice is an example of a cereal grain

explanation.surface: A claim that the humble grain hosts a clever Briton.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe things of the mind and intellect rather than the emotions or body.

clue.text: Some put on a lesson of sound quality

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A teacher staging a class about how things sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonal is the adjective for tone, the character or quality of a musical sound.

clue.text: Fluorine untraceable, it's said, in treated teeth

indicators.note: it's said marks a word heard rather than read, here the spoken pair

parts.note: F is the chemical symbol for fluorine; something untraceable is lost

explanation.surface: Dental fluoride has vanished from the teeth a dentist worked on.
explanation.definitionFit: To floss is to clean between the teeth with thread, a way of treating them.

clue.text: Finished work at the office, here

definitions.text: Finished work at the office, here

parts.words: Finished work at the office, here
parts.note: completed office paperwork is placed in a tray marked for collection and dispatch

explanation.surface: An instruction about where to put completed office paperwork.
explanation.definitionFit: The tray on a desk for dealt-with documents waiting to be collected is labelled for outgoing items.

clue.text: The brontosaurus, half ruined, in old storehouse

indicators.note: half of the dinosaur's name is destroyed, leaving only its second half

explanation.surface: A dinosaur skeleton, half wrecked, kept in an ancient warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half ruined' wrecks the front half of the dinosaur's twelve-letter name, the BRONTO part; the old sense of storehouse is the word's Greek origin, a treasury.
explanation.definitionFit: The word originally meant a treasury or storehouse, before it came to mean a store of words.

clue.text: Rich man takes drugs to get started

indicators.note: the rich man takes in the drugs, holding them inside

parts.note: a toff is a wealthy, upper-class man in British slang
E is slang for ecstasy, so two of them make EE

explanation.surface: A wealthy man turns to narcotics to get himself going.
explanation.walkthrough: TOFF is British slang for a posh, wealthy person.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, playing the first shot begins the round, so the phrase came to mean begin.

clue.text: Go carefully with advice to egghead

parts.note: a tip is a piece of advice
the head, or first letter, of egg is E

explanation.surface: Counsel offered to an intellectual about treading carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking on the balls of the feet is moving quietly and cautiously.

clue.text: A car for the Italian summer

explanation.walkthrough: An estate car is the British name for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: The British term for a long-backed family car, and also the season's name in Italian.

clue.text: Insurer unable to cover race again

indicators.note: the outer words cover, or contain, the letters sought

explanation.surface: An insurer cannot provide cover for a horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a race once more is to run it again.

clue.text: Where cream may go straight away

definitions.meaning: a dab of ointment is applied to a pimple

explanation.walkthrough: Spot here is a pimple, the place where spot cream is applied.
explanation.definitionFit: Ointment goes on a pimple, and the idiom for acting there and then means immediately.

clue.text: Blue rinse, restyle then spray

indicators.note: restyling rearranges, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A hairdresser's routine: blue rinse, restyle, then hairspray.
explanation.definitionFit: A nebuliser is a device turning liquid medicine into a fine mist to inhale.

clue.text: Jack or Tom's first to pull the plug

parts.note: a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the word Tom's

explanation.surface: Asking which of two men will be first to cancel something.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull the plug on a plan is to stop it before completion, to call it off.

clue.text: A bride's crazy one might follow a wake

indicators.note: crazy means mixed up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A bride is wild enough to follow a funeral wake.
explanation.walkthrough: The wake looks like a funeral gathering; it is the trail of water behind a ship, which gulls follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Gulls and other ocean birds trail behind ships in the churned water they leave.

clue.text: Master forger identified in press: a well-known name

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
Smith is the commonest surname in Britain

explanation.surface: A master counterfeiter outed in the newspapers as someone famous.
explanation.definitionFit: A forger here is one who works a forge, and a skilled blacksmith shapes iron there.

clue.text: Cart backs up a few feet

indicators.note: in a down-the-page reading backing up turns the word round

parts.note: a dray is a low, heavy cart

explanation.surface: A wagon reverses a short distance.
explanation.definitionFit: This unit of length equals three feet, a handful of them.

clue.text: Rainbow's colours are all seen in pearl, strangely

indicators.note: strangely means oddly arranged, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Every rainbow hue shows in the sheen of a pearl.
explanation.definitionFit: The bands of a rainbow run side by side, never meeting, in equally spaced lines.

clue.text: Did he refuse to go 1 across?

definitions.text: Did he refuse to go 1 across?

parts.words: Did he refuse to go 1 across?
parts.note: the cross-reference means returning to the front line after leave

explanation.surface: Asking whether a soldier declined to rejoin the battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 across reads here as 'back to the front', where a soldier on leave should return.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier who runs off and will not return to duty is an absconder from the army.

clue.text: Low investment finally up for discussion

parts.note: to low is to moo, the sound cattle make

indicators.note: finally takes only the closing letter of investment

explanation.surface: A small stake raised at last as a topic for a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A moot point is one open to debate, still to be argued over.

clue.text: Empress's soldiers guarding nerve gas

definitions.note: the 's is 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: the soldiers stand around the gas, enclosing it

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
sarin is a nerve agent

explanation.surface: An empress's troops protect a stock of chemical weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: The wife of a tsar, or a Russian empress in her own right.

clue.text: Scoundrel, boxed in, falls in the river

indicators.note: in here means placed inside, so the scoundrel sits within the box word

parts.note: boxed suggests a box, or case
a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A villain, confined, plunges into the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a small waterfall, a series of drops in a stream's course.

clue.text: Many pointless clues need editing — that's insulting!

indicators.note: editing reworks text, so the letters are rearranged
the compass points E and S are removed from the word clues

explanation.surface: A solver complaining that a setter's aimless clues need revising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointless' strips the compass points E and S from CLUES, leaving CLU to be mixed with MANY.
explanation.definitionFit: Calumny is slander, a false and damaging statement meant as an insult.

clue.text: Emperor Michael's brief song and dance

indicators.note: brief cuts the last letter off the short form of the name

parts.note: Mike is the short form of Michael
a song and dance is a fuss, or ado

explanation.surface: An emperor's dancing and singing, given a short name.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mikado is the title for the Emperor of Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mikado is an old title for the emperor of Japan.

clue.text: Turn away Polish — again!

parts.note: RE is a prefix meaning again
to buff is to polish

explanation.surface: An instruction to send someone off, then shine it all over again.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebuff is to reject or snub, turning someone away.

clue.text: Theories said to be mistaken about energy

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the energy symbol
mistaken means wrongly ordered, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Notions reported to be wrong concerning energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistaken' scrambles SAID into IDAS, which goes about E.
explanation.definitionFit: Theories and notions are both thoughts put forward to explain something.

clue.text: Quits everything conservative

parts.note: all means everything
a square is an old-fashioned, conventional person

explanation.surface: Someone abandons all things traditional.
explanation.definitionFit: Being even, with no debt outstanding, is being quits.

clue.text: Leave nothing as capital

parts.note: to quit is to leave
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Advice to abandon everything for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Quito is the capital city of Ecuador.

clue.text: Alloy's 40% metal

parts.note: the first two of the five letters of alloy are the chemical symbol of this metal

explanation.surface: A metallurgist states the proportion of one metal in an alloy.
explanation.walkthrough: 40% of ALLOY is AL, the chemical symbol for the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: The light silvery element with symbol Al, widely used in alloys.

clue.text: Scrabble tiles spelling "inch"

indicators.note: scrabbling tiles about mixes them, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Scrabble tiles laid out to form a word.
explanation.walkthrough: Inch is a Scottish word for a small island.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland and Ireland an inch is a small island, a little isle.

clue.text: See 7
One should ensure a level playing-field

definitions.text: One should ensure a level playing-field

parts.words: One should ensure a level playing-field
parts.note: the fairness idiom is read literally as flattening a sports pitch

explanation.surface: A call for fair competition.
explanation.walkthrough: A heavy roller is used to flatten a cricket pitch before play.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundstaff run a big weighted roller over a cricket pitch to make it flat.
